In GAMA-Bench, the 405B Llama-3.1 model performs worse than the 70B version because it is described as overly conservative, i.e., the larger model’s caution hurts performance.

By contrast, the K-Level Reasoning paper concludes that the K-R framework improves strategic reasoning by enabling recursive higher-order belief modeling. It reports advantages of K-R on its testbeds, but it does not make the same kind of claim that a smaller/weaker model using K-R outperforms a larger base model like GPT-4 under direct prompting. Instead, the contribution is that the framework itself improves the model’s reasoning ability through recursion.

So the contrast is: GAMA-Bench shows a larger model can do worse than a smaller one due to an overly conservative policy, whereas K-Level Reasoning shows that adding the K-R framework can strengthen strategic reasoning, but not that a smaller model with K-R necessarily surpasses GPT-4 with plain prompting.
